( 01 )THE THROUGHLINE

A scientist’s
curiosity.

My work revolves around a central question: how can we make learning systems more reliable and actionable when real-world data are complex, sparse, and biased?

From offline meta-reinforcement learning to protein engineering, I build AI models that are generalizable, controllable and interpretable, with the ultimate goal to accelerate scientific discovery, making translational impact especially in biomedicine.

( 03 )SELECTED WORK

Ideas that
travel.

A few projects that show how the questions evolved—from decision making to molecular modeling.

2027 · PreprintNew manuscript

Label-Free Fine-Tuning

A post-training method that leverages intrinsic and extrinsic reward signal—without requiring labeled preference data.

Read the paper ↗
2026 · Nature CommunicationsIn vitro validated

DeepDelivery

AI-driven discovery and engineering of human-derived protein scaffolds for mRNA delivery. The platform surfaced 12 of 15 novel materials with delivery activity in vitro.

Read the paper ↗
2026 · Acta Pharmaceutica Sinica BEditor’s Highlight

ERAM

A task-agnostic framework that connects substrates, enzymes, and products in a shared molecular representation space. Multimodal relational learning supports enzyme retrieval, substrate prediction, and binding-site analysis.

Read the paper ↗
2024 · NeurIPS SpotlightTop 2.47%

UNICORN

An information-theoretic framework that unifies context-based offline meta-RL and paves a principled path towards foundation models for decision making.

Read the paper ↗
2023 · CVPRLong-tailed recognition

CC-SAM

A robust optimization method for long-tailed visual recognition. PAC-Bayesian analysis motives class-conditional parameter perturbations that encourage flatter minima in the loss landscape.

Read the paper ↗

( 05 )THE JOURNEY

A computer scientist and physicist
by training.

Physics taught me to seek nature’s underlying structure and principles. Machine learning gave me the tools to test them.

I’m an incoming postdoctoral scholar in Bioengineering at Stanford Medicine, working with Prof. Le Cong and Prof. Mengdi Wang (Princeton). Before that, I led AIDD research at Zhejiang Lab and Tencent AI Lab. I was fortunate to complete my PhD under the supervision of Prof. Pheng-Ann Heng at CUHK.
